change.author: Alan

findings.title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty or null and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` gives `undefined` when there is no destination calendar. Line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without `?.`, so it throws. This PR makes `[]` the default for many callers (bookingReminder, webhook, confirm and others), and handleNewBooking can pass `null`. Before, `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` fell back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references lose their credentialId
findings.body: The old code set `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video references kept the video credential id. The new code sets `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so every non-calendar reference is stored without a credentialId. Later paths that look up the credential by reference (for example deleting or updating a video meeting) lose it silently. Use `result.credentialId` for both branches.

findings.title: updateLocation stores undefined externalCalendarId and applies it to video results
findings.body: `result.externalId` is only set by `CalendarManager.createEvent` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:267). `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not return it, and video results never have it. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. So after editing a location, the new calendar references get `externalCalendarId` undefined, and later update or delete calls fall back to the default calendar. Carry the reference's externalCalendarId through the update result.

findings.title: Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent can never match
findings.body: This line is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` then compares against a falsy value, so it almost never matches and the result is `undefined`. The old fallback was `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. The same problem is at line 317 in deleteEvent. For references with no externalCalendarId, such as old bookings, the update or delete goes to the primary calendar instead of the destination calendar. Use the first destination calendar, or one matched by credentialId.

findings.title: Recurring-delete block now runs once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring branch deletes events for every remaining booking across all of the user's calendar credentials. It now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, so with N calendar references the same deletions run N times. The repeats are API calls that fail or double-delete. Run that branch once, outside the loop.

findings.title: Dynamic-group user select drops organization slug
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` select for the no-eventTypeId case no longer includes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. It also drops the `// Don't leak to client` comment on `credentials`. Code that reads `user.organization?.slug` for dynamic bookings will now get undefined. This is unrelated to the PR's purpose. Restore the select.

findings.title: Collective destination calendars are pushed after an async map
findings.body: `teamDestinationCalendars` is filled inside async `.map` callbacks. This works today only because the callbacks push before their first await. Compute it synchronously instead. Also, the booking stores only `destinationCalendar[0]` (line 1877). Other services (Lark, Office365, CalDAV) read only the first entry, so teammates' calendars are ignored there.

findings.title: Slug condition inverted for organization creation
findings.body: The original code set `slug` when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. The new line 151 is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which sets it when billing is enabled. The `requestedSlug` condition on line 153 is unchanged, so with billing on both `slug` and `requestedSlug` are set. With billing off, the org gets no slug at all. This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar work. Restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, or drop the change.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 1.** The multi-destination-calendar refactor has one crash and several regressions. EventManager.ts:119 throws when destinationCalendar is empty, which the PR now makes the default. Video references lose their credentialId. updateLocation stores an undefined externalCalendarId. The Google update/delete fallback lookup can never match. The recurring cancel branch repeats once per calendar reference. The dynamic-user select also dropped the organization slug. I read only the relevant parts of EventManager.ts and CalendarManager.ts. I did not open the other files in full, so the findings on Google, handleCancelBooking and handleNewBooking rest on the diff alone, which is why some are medium confidence.

**Batch 1 of 1, retry.** The destinationCalendar array conversions in this part are consistent across the call sites I checked. One blocker: the unrelated change in organizations/create.handler.ts inverts the `slug` condition.
